title: How the Term Was Written: Retention Multiplier on a Named Insured's Cancellation (Named Non-Owner Policy)
content:
**Q. What does the origin of a Named Non-Owner Policy term change on a cancellation at the named insured's request?**
It sets a multiplier of the package's insured-cancellation retention percentage, applied to that percentage before the reduction is taken.

**Q. How is the origin read?**
From the reason on the term's latest premium-written entry; when two such entries share the latest processing date, the one recorded first is read.

**Q. What are the multipliers?**
- A new-business term multiplies the retention by 1.25.
- A renewal term on which a lapse is recorded, so that it was accepted after its expiring term's expiration, multiplies it by 1.10.
- A renewal accepted on time, or a term with no premium-written entry, leaves it unchanged.

| Latest premium-written entry's reason | Lapse recorded on the term | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| new business | — | 1.25 |
| renewal | yes | 1.10 |
| renewal | no | none |
| no premium-written entry | — | none |

**Q. A term has a premium-written entry for new business dated 3 February and another for renewal dated 3 February recorded later. Which one counts?**
They share the latest processing date, so the one recorded first — new business — is read (hypothetical).
